The confidence interval widths grow substantially as the horizon extends, which reflects the well-established principle that uncertainty compounds over time. By one week, the interval widens to 44 points, incorporating the possibility of several consecutive adverse sessions or a sudden repricing event. At one month, the interval expands to 95 points, reflecting the full range of macro developments, earnings cycles, policy shifts, or sentiment changes that could materialize over roughly 20 trading days.

Specific risks that could push outcomes outside these intervals include sudden macroeconomic data surprises — such as an unexpected inflation print, central bank policy shift, or geopolitical shock — that could gap the price well beyond either tail. A sharp risk-off episode driven by credit stress, a liquidity event, or an unforeseen geopolitical escalation could push the one-month outcome well below 360. It is also worth acknowledging the inherent limitation that these forecasts are generated without real-time data feeds, so the starting price assumption and recent trend context carry some uncertainty themselves. If the asset had already made a significant move just prior to this forecast being issued, the actual distribution of outcomes could be shifted materially in either direction relative to what I have described here.
